key_insight: Continual-learning adapters work best when specialized in intermediate transformer blocks, and this placement can be found without search by using brain-readout signals from early tasks.
engineering_relevance: The method cuts adapter storage growth while preserving accuracy, offering a practical way to place task-specific capacity in vision transformers with minimal compute and no labels.
method: Search all contiguous four-block adapter placements to map where accuracy peaks across depth.
Use frozen fMRI encoding readouts from twelve visual areas to score how task-varying each block is.
Commit capacity once to the blocks with the strongest cross-task variation and lowest structural stability.
evidence_signal: Across three ViT-B/16 backbones, LS-B consistently selected intermediate-depth blocks and on Split ImageNet-R used 60% of full-BiLoRA storage while staying within 1.5 percentage points of final accuracy.
watch_item: The allocation is backbone-specific and depends on early-task observations, so portability to new architectures or shifted task streams may require re-validation.
paper_title: Two Routes to the Middle: Placement Search and Brain Readouts Converge on Where Continual Learners Should Specialize
